settings.planningNotes: Two people. Lunch is batch-cooked: 6 servings per batch (2 per person x 3 days), two batches cover Mon-Sat. Dinner is cooked once for 4 servings and eaten as leftovers the next day. Breakfast is simple: overnight oats prepped the night before, eggs & toast same-day, pancakes optional. Keep everything mild; add heat after cooking (red pepper flakes on the side). No mushrooms, no pork, no seafood beyond tuna and salmon; beef only as ground beef.

recipes.title: Easy Slow Cooker Chili
recipes.description: A hearty, rich crockpot chili with ground beef, two kinds of kidney beans, and warm spices. The slow cooker does most of the work.
recipes.author: Jaclyn
recipes.storageNotes: Refrigerate in airtight containers up to 4 days; freezes well up to 3 months.
recipes.notes: Household makes this mild: use diced tomatoes with MILD green chilies and pass red pepper flakes on the side. Ingredient quantities are for 8 servings; the lunch batch is scaled to 6.

ingredients.originalText: 2 (14.5 oz) cans diced tomatoes with green chilies
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
1 (15 oz) can dark red kidney beans, drained and rinsed
1 (15 oz) can light red kidney beans, drained and rinsed

steps.text: Heat the olive oil in a large, deep non-stick skillet over medium-high heat. Add the onion and saute 3 minutes, then add the garlic and saute 30 seconds longer. Scrape the onions and garlic into a 6- or 7-quart slow cooker.
Return the skillet to medium-high heat, add the beef, and cook, stirring occasionally, until browned.
Drain most of the fat, leaving about 2 Tbsp in the pan (optional), and add the beef to the slow cooker.
Stir in the diced tomatoes, tomato sauce, beef broth, chili powder, cumin, paprika, cocoa powder, sugar, and coriander. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Cover and cook on low heat for 5-6 hours.
Stir in the dark and light red kidney beans and heat through, about 2 minutes.
Serve warm with shredded cheddar and any other desired toppings.

recipes.title: Lazy Slow Cooker Chicken Soup
recipes.description: Golden chicken broth with carrots, turnips, parsnips, and fresh herbs. Minimal effort, comfort food in a bowl.
recipes.author: Susan Goldenberg
recipes.storageNotes: Refrigerate in an airtight container 3-5 days; freeze 4-6 months. Reheat single servings gently.
recipes.notes: Source recipe is 10 servings; the plan scales the lunch batch to 6. Roasted garlic gives a mellow flavor, but regular garlic cloves can be substituted. Bone-in chicken pieces add flavor; add noodles or rice to make it heartier.

ingredients.prepNote: boneless skinless; bone-in pieces add flavor

ingredients.originalText: 2 celery stalks, cut in large pieces

steps.text: Place the chicken pieces in the bottom of a 6-quart (or larger) slow cooker.
Add the carrots, celery, turnips, parsnips, garlic, and onion.
Pour in the chicken stock.
Lay the dill and rosemary sprigs on top. Cover and cook on low 6-8 hours (or on high for 4 hours).
Remove the herb sprigs. Pull out the chicken, shred it with two forks, and return as much as desired to the pot (about half keeps plenty of broth). Season with salt and pepper to taste.

recipes.title: Marry Me Chicken Pasta
recipes.description: Tender chicken and penne tossed in a creamy sun-dried tomato and parmesan sauce. Ready in 30 minutes.
recipes.author: Alyssa Rivers
recipes.storageNotes: Refrigerate tightly covered up to 4 days. Reheat gently on the stove or microwave with a splash of cream.
recipes.notes: Household keeps this mild: skip added heat in the sauce and pass red pepper flakes at the table if desired. Uses sun-dried tomatoes, not canned tomatoes. Use freshly grated parmesan for the best melt.

ingredients.originalText: 1 1/2 pounds boneless skinless chicken, cut into 1-inch pieces

steps.text: Cook the penne according to package directions. Drain and set aside.
Cut the chicken into 1-inch pieces and season with the salt and pepper.
Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the chicken and cook 6-8 minutes, until no longer pink and cooked through.
Transfer the chicken to a plate and set aside.
Return the skillet to the heat and melt the butter. Saute the garlic 30 seconds until fragrant, then stir in the flour to make a paste.
Whisk in the chicken broth, heavy cream, and parmesan cheese.
Stir in the drained sun-dried tomatoes, paprika, and Italian seasoning. Season with more salt and pepper if needed.
Simmer the sauce a few minutes so it can thicken.
Return the chicken and cooked pasta to the skillet and stir to coat everything in the sauce.
Garnish with chopped basil and additional parmesan, then serve.

recipes.title: Mediterranean Salmon Sheet Pan Dinner
recipes.description: Skinless salmon roasted on one sheet pan with zucchini, red pepper, potato, olives, and lemon. Gluten-free and dairy-free.
recipes.author: Gina Homolka
recipes.storageNotes: Refrigerate up to 3 days. Reheat 30-60 seconds in the microwave, or 5-10 minutes in a 325F oven.
recipes.notes: Salmon is explicitly allowed by the household seafood rule. Cut the onion, bell pepper, and zucchini the day before to speed up prep. A second sheet pan can be used to double the vegetables.

ingredients.originalText: 1 medium zucchini, cut into 1/2-inch thick rounds
1 red bell pepper, stem and seeds removed and sliced
1 small red onion, cut into chunks
8 ounces white potato, from 1 large potato, cut into 1/2-inch thick rounds and halved

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 425F and line a rimmed baking sheet with parchment paper.
Toss the zucchini, bell pepper, red onion, and potato in a mixing bowl with olive oil, salt, pepper, garlic powder, dried parsley, and dried oregano. Spread in an even layer on the baking sheet.
Roast the vegetables for 20 minutes, until partially cooked but not completely tender.
Meanwhile, drizzle the salmon fillets with olive oil and season with sweet paprika, garlic powder, salt, and pepper.
Remove the pan from the oven and shift the vegetables aside to make room. Add the salmon, top each fillet with olives, and roast 15 minutes more, until the fish flakes easily with a fork.
Serve the salmon with the roasted vegetables and lemon wedges.

recipes.title: Ground Beef and Broccoli
recipes.description: A 30-minute ground beef and broccoli stir-fry in a sweet-savory soy sauce, served over rice.
recipes.author: Stephanie
recipes.storageNotes: Refrigerate in an airtight container up to 3 days; freeze up to 3 months.
recipes.notes: Household keeps this mild; use low-sodium soy sauce if sodium is a concern and pass red pepper flakes on the side. Peanut oil can be replaced with vegetable or olive oil. Ground beef is the only beef cut used.

ingredients.prepNote: can sub vegetable or olive oil
ingredients.originalText: 1 Tablespoon peanut oil, can sub vegetable or olive
3 cups broccoli florets, washed and patted dry

ingredients.prepNote: start with 1 Tbsp, add more to taste
cooked; about 1 cup dry yields 3 cups

steps.text: Stir the cornstarch and cold water together in a covered container and set aside. Combine the beef broth, soy sauce, brown sugar, honey, garlic, ginger, and sesame oil in a bowl.
Heat the oil over medium heat. Add the broccoli and toss to coat; cook 4-5 minutes until slightly softened. Remove and set aside.

Season the beef with salt and white pepper. Cook and crumble the ground beef and onion over medium-high heat until browned and cooked through. Drain the grease, add the sliced bell pepper, and cook 1 minute.
Add the sauce mixture and bring to a gentle boil. Simmer and reduce 2-3 minutes, then shake the cornstarch mixture and stir it in slowly until the sauce reaches the desired thickness.
Reduce the heat to low, return the broccoli, and stir to combine and heat through. Serve over rice, garnished with green onions if desired.

recipes.title: Overnight Oats
recipes.description: Creamy no-cook oats soaked overnight with milk, chia, and honey. Ready when you wake up.
recipes.storageNotes: Keeps up to 3 days in the fridge. Stir and loosen with a splash of milk before eating; eat cold or reheat.
recipes.notes: Household breakfast for Mon/Wed/Fri; the cook event is dated the evening before. Top with fruit, nuts, or a spoonful of yogurt if available.

steps.text: Divide the oats, milk, chia seeds, honey, vanilla, and a pinch of salt between two jars.
Stir well, cover, and refrigerate at least 6 hours or overnight.
Stir before eating, loosen with a splash of milk if thick, and add toppings.

recipes.title: Eggs & Toast
recipes.description: Soft-scrambled eggs with buttered toast, the weekday breakfast standby.
recipes.storageNotes: Best eaten fresh; refrigerate leftovers up to 1 day.
recipes.notes: Saturday variation: pancakes optional instead of (or alongside) eggs & toast. Sunday breakfast may be eggs & toast or oats.

steps.text: Toast the bread.
Beat the eggs with a pinch of salt and pepper.
Melt the butter in a non-stick skillet over medium-low heat. Add the eggs and stir gently until just set, about 3-4 minutes.
Pile the eggs onto the toast and season with more pepper if desired.

recipes.title: Pancakes
recipes.description: Fluffy everyday pancakes made from pantry staples.
recipes.storageNotes: Refrigerate leftovers up to 2 days; reheat in the toaster or a dry skillet.
recipes.notes: Optional Saturday breakfast; the plan keeps eggs & toast as the default. Serve with butter and syrup or honey.

steps.text: Whisk the flour, baking powder, sugar, and salt in a bowl.
Whisk the milk, egg, melted butter, and vanilla in a second bowl, then pour into the dry ingredients and stir until just combined (lumps are fine).
Heat a lightly greased griddle or skillet over medium heat. Pour about 1/4 cup batter per pancake and cook until bubbles form and the edges look set, about 2 minutes; flip and cook 1-2 minutes more.
Serve warm with butter and syrup or honey.
